correctness.rationale: The local Gauss-sum proof explicitly verifies all valuations including zero delay, and the unit-coefficient assumption supplies the needed nondegeneracy. Exact CRT tensor multiplicities and a normalization derivation establish the full operator spectrum and Weyl kernel. Odd-length nearest-neighbor ratios prove nonlinear uniqueness; a Poincaré inequality proves the flat-signal lower bound. Standalone independent FFT/Gram checks at seven moduli and direct intensity checks at three moduli succeeded; these checks do not replace universal proof.

value.rationale: The arithmetic spectrum determines every identifiable and missing operator direction for a natural measurement family, not merely a binary invertibility test. It distinguishes prime from composite off-diagonal blindness, quantifies an asymptotically vanishing rank fraction, and simultaneously proves that all full-support signals remain identifiable, with an explicit flat-signal stability constant. This contrast between linear and restricted nonlinear identifiability has direct structural mathematical content.
